Triage: lands in the objectui console's domains page ⇒ **`domain:ui`**; rationale below.

**Type `Feature`, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue` → `pm:blocked`.**

## Domain

objectui splits three ways: `domain:devx` (engineering surface), `domain:spec` (contract surface), and everything else — the shipped libraries and apps — to `domain:ui`. An operator-facing wizard on the domains page is squarely the third. ⇒ `domain:ui`.

## Why `pm:blocked`, and why that is a reading rather than a verdict

The body already declares `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/cloud#2136`, and the card says the control-plane half is "landing in objectstack-ai/cloud PR #2152" — i.e. in flight at filing time, not merged.

⚠️ **I could not measure it.** This session's GitHub access is scoped to `objectstack-ai/objectstack` and `objectstack-ai/objectui`; `objectstack-ai/cloud` is unreachable from here, and the global `/search/issues` endpoint is refused for the same reason (`403 — sessions are bound to their configured repositories`). ⛔ An unreachable repo is not a clean check, so I am not recording one.

⇒ `pm:blocked` is the honest state: the blocker is declared, unmerged as far as anything on this card says, and unmeasurable from this seat. It is **not** a finding that the work is unready.

## Ready-made command for the cloud seat — please paste the reading back onto this card

```
gh issue view 2136 --repo objectstack-ai/cloud --json number,state,stateReason,closedAt
gh pr view 2152 --repo objectstack-ai/cloud --json number,state,merged,mergedAt,mergeCommit
```

**The reading that flips this card:** cloud#2136 closed **and** PR #2152 merged **and** the endpoints reachable on the deployed control plane — the cross-repo unlock criterion is *the consumer can actually call it*, ⛔ not merely that the upstream merged. Until all three hold, this stays blocked; when they do, it goes back to `pm:queue` with the file surface re-verified on the merged ref.

`priority:p2`: a real capability shipped Team-and-above with no way for an operator to reach it, which is worse than not having shipped it — but no existing flow is broken, so not p1.

`Feature` by the type rule: it enlarges the operator-facing surface. ⛔ That does **not** put it in the decision box — the shape is not a proposal, it is dictated by a control plane that already implemented and shipped it (three steps, the `verification` object's `record_name`/`record_type`/`record_value`, `cname_target`, and the `pending_verification → verified → provisioning → active` machine with `failed`/`suspended`). The decision was taken upstream; this is its consequence.

Ruling: batch #198 item 2 · letter A · maintainer 「同意」 2026-09-20T12:03Z

Director seat, summon #25, `session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`. Presented in detail with the recommendation **A** (close; fallback B park; C offered explicitly if cloud-side customers were waiting); the maintainer agreed 「同意」. Thread re-read to its last comment (5621222905) in the act that wrote this.

## Ruling — A: closed, not planned

- The console does not build the BYO custom-hostname wizard page (three steps, live status, Free-plan upgrade prompt) in this repo now. `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` 〈现在不做〉: 「云服务的旅程(注册、控制面、托管)另有自己的清单 … 计费未建」; 〈优先级〉 rule 2: 「不在路上、不在清单上 ⇒ p3 或不做」. The measured checklist (`docs/qa/platform-checklist/`, 15 areas, 264 items) carries no custom-domain, hosting or plan-tier entry, so 「not on the list」 is a reading.
- The cloud-side capability (objectstack-ai/cloud#2136: control plane, verification, certificate issuance, `pending_verification → verified → provisioning → active` with `failed` / `suspended`) is untouched by this ruling and stays as shipped; only the self-service console page is not built here.
- **Reopen is free**, on either of two readings, and this comment is the reopen condition: (1) the cloud journey's operator surfaces enter this repo's checklist (a hosting / custom-domain area in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/`), or (2) a named customer on Team-or-above is waiting for the self-service wizard — the reading this seat could not take from here. Whoever reopens states which.
- **B refused** as the primary (a parked card with a file-touch trigger is legal but buys nothing over a free reopen); **C refused** (a console surface with no checklist entry and no owner, coupled to a state machine that lives in another repo).

Four-facet reading (this seat's own): ① A shrinks the exception — this repo's road and checklist are 「an application built on the protocol」; ② ⛔ not measurable from this repo: the pull is known only cloud-side and to sales, recorded as the gap that flips this to C, ⛔ not written as zero; ③ neutral — no writable metadata surface changes under any option; ④ every declared surface is a permanent obligation, and this one would have to follow cloud's state machine with no reminder mechanism.

`Prior rulings read: custom domain, hostname, cloud journey, billing, plan tier → ADR-0068 D4 (billing override as an isPlatformAdmin example — does not govern which repo owns the cloud journey's surface); NORTH-STAR 〈现在不做〉 quoted above.`

## Execution, same stroke

Closed `not_planned`; `needs-user-decision` removed in the same stroke (closing removes the pm-state label); `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` stay (ownership, not state). The `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/cloud#2136` body line stays as the card's provenance and is inert on a closed card.
